rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate raises aggressiveness across all seven passes: SecurityGain and DiversityGain are pushed high everywhere to maximize resistance on this tiny (4-function, ~1.1KB text) bit-manipulation benchmark whose small hot functions (ReverseBits32/64, main) tolerate substantial transformation; SUB and IBR get the strongest weights since arithmetic and block-level indirection are cheap, broadly applicable, and hard to reverse; BCF, ICALL, and FLA follow closely, with FLA tempered slightly because the suite is float-heavy (fbench/flops-style code) and control-flow flattening interacts poorly with tight numeric loops; SPLIT is kept at moderate-high weights since its cost is mostly size and this binary has ample headroom; IGV carries the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.3) because global-variable reordering is the most likely pass to perturb the bit-reversal lookup semantics, and its gains overlap with SUB/BCF. RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights sit in the 0.4-0.7 band: high enough that cost-tolerant small functions still qualify for passes, but below the security dimensions so overhead remains bounded and correctness is preserved as in round 0.
